senses.gloss: युध् [cf. Zd. yud; Gk. ὑσ-μίνη.]
2. युध् m. a fighter, warrior, hero, MBh.; Hariv.
यु॑ध् f. war, fight, combat, struggle, contest, RV.; &c.
युधा instr. of 2. युध्, in comp.
युधा—जि m. (prob. for -जित्; but cf. यौधाजय) N. of a man (v.l. युद्धाजि).
युधा—जित् mfn. conquering or vanquishing by means of war, PañcavBr.; MBh.
N. of a son of Kroṣṭu by a woman called Mādrī, Hariv.
of a son of Kekaya (uncle of Bharata), R.
of a son of Vṛṣṇi, VP.
of a king of Ujjayinī, Cat.
युधा—जीव m. (w.r. for युद्धाज्˚ ?) N. of a man.
युधा—मन्यु m. N. of a warrior on the side of the Pāṇḍavas, MBh.; BhP.
युधा—सुर m. (w.r. for युद्धास्˚ ?) N. of a king.
युधां-श्रौष्टि m. N. of a man, AitBr.
युधान m. a man of the second or military order, a warrior, W.
an enemy, Uṇ. ii, 90, Sch.
1. युधि fighting, battle (only in dat. युध॑ये; see under √ 1. युध्).
2. युधि loc. of 2. युध्, in comp.
युधि—ं-गम mfn. going to battle, AV.

युधि—ष्ठिर m. (for -स्थिर) ‘firm or steady in battle’, N. of the eldest of the 5 reputed sons of Pāṇḍu (really the child of Pṛthā or Kuntī, Pāṇḍu's wife, by the god Dharma or Yama, whence he is often called Dharma-putra or Dharma-rāja; he ultimately succeeded Pāṇḍu as king, first reigning over Indra-prastha, and afterwards, when the Kuru princes were defeated, at Hastinā-pura; cf. IW. 379 &c.), MBh.; Hariv.; Pur.
of a son of Kṛṣṇa, Hariv.
of two kings of Kaśmīra, Rājat.
of a potter, Pañcat.
(with महोपाध्याय) of a preceptor, Cat.
pl. the descendants of Yudhiṣṭhira (son of Pāṇḍu), Pāṇ. ii, 4, 66, Sch.
युधि—ष्ठिर—विजय m. (or -दिग्-व्˚) N. of a poem by Vāsudeva Parama-śiva-yogin of Kerala.
युधिक mfn. fighting, contending, L.
युधे॑न्य mfn. to be fought with, to be overcome in battle, RV.
युध्म॑ m. a warrior, hero, RV.
(only L.) a battle
an arrow
a bow
= शेष-संग्राम
= शरभ.
युध्यामधि॑ m. N. of a man, RV. vii, 18, 24.
यु॑ध्वन् mfn. warlike, martial, a warrior, RV.
